subject: Request: SLO carveout + one-time credit for high-throughput pilot
messages:
From: Claire Thompson <claire@orbitalanalytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@orbitalanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot SLO request and onboarding pricing

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the throughput and the prefix caching behavior. We're preparing a high-volume pilot (internal analytics workloads, mostly short prompts) that will run for ~16 weeks and would like to finalize commercial terms this week. Two asks from our side: 

1) SLO carveout: For the pilot period we'd like the uptime SLO set to 99.5% (rather than Redwood's standard 99.9%). This is a hard constraint for our compliance team for the initial pilot.
2) One-time commercial concession: a transitional onboarding credit applied to the first invoice (we're proposing 15% of first-month committed spend).

We expect token volume to be spiky during training runs — see attached latency_report_q1.csv for projected burst windows. Also attached is our proposed SOW (Orbital_SOW_v3.pdf).

We understand these are non-standard; if there are guardrails or telemetry requirements Redwood needs to operate under (rollback triggers, additional monitoring hooks), please let us know. We're aiming to sign this week.

Claire
Claire Thompson
Head of Platform Partnerships
Orbital Analytics
Attachments: Orbital_SOW_v3.pdf, latency_report_q1.csv
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot SLO request and onboarding pricing

Team — forwarding Orbital's asks. TL;DR: 16-week pilot, wants 99.5% SLO for pilot, plus one-time 15% onboarding credit. Volume will be bursty and may stress KV cache warmup. Attached latency report looks plausible.

Options I see (recommend we keep to an explicit, auditable exception):

A) Approve temporary SLO change to 99.5% for up to 4 months with these constraints: monthly telemetry export to Redwood, automatic rollback to 99.9% if error-rate > X (we should define), and a capped service-credit exposure of $50k for the pilot. Offer a 10-15% one-time onboarding credit (needs finance signoff).

B) Decline the SLO change, keep 99.9% but offer a commercial concession (e.g., larger credit or accelerated support) to get the deal done.

Questions for you: what maximum service-credit exposure are we comfortable with for a pilot? Is a 15% onboarding credit acceptable from a margin perspective, or should we cap at 12%?

I'm happy to escalate to VP commercial for explicit authority if needed. Orbital is in our US strategic pipeline and wants to sign quickly.

Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: internal: pilot_exposure_calc.xlsx (not shared externally)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot SLO request and onboarding pricing

Vivek — thanks for the clear summary. I ran the numbers with finance overnight. Key concerns:

- Exposure: based on their projected bursts, worst-case service-credit liability could exceed $120k if we leave the SLO uncapped. We should definitely cap liability or require a spend- or token-based ceiling.
- Precedent: approving 99.5% as a formal SLO for a paying customer sets a precedent we should record (Deal Desk + Legal must capture clause language).
- Telemetry: require a weekly telemetry feed with agreed-on KPIs (p99 latency, error-rate, prefix-cache hit-rate) and an explicit auto-rollback trigger if p99 exceeds 800ms for 3 consecutive days.

Recommendation: escalate for VP commercial signoff with a concrete proposal: 99.5% SLO for up to 16 weeks, cap cumulative service-credit exposure at $50k, one-time onboarding credit of 12% (compromise), and mandatory telemetry + automatic rollback clause. Also require the SOW be updated and DocuSign routed to Legal for redlines.

Deal ID: ORB-2027-019

If we get VP signoff I'll draft the amendment language and route to Legal.

Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Desk Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot SLO request and onboarding pricing — VP approval

Team / Vivek — after reviewing the exposure analysis and the strategic importance of Orbital, I approve the following limited exception: 

1) SLO: Temporarily set uptime SLO to 99.5% for the defined pilot period (maximum 16 weeks). This is an exception and must be explicitly labeled in the contract amendment.
2) Service-credit cap: Set cumulative service-credit liability for the pilot at $50,000. Any credits above that amount require my written approval.
3) Commercial concession: Approve a one-time onboarding credit of 12% applied to the first invoice.
4) Guardrails: Require weekly telemetry exports (p99 latency, error rates, cache hit rate). Insert an automatic rollback clause: if p99 latency > 800ms for 3 consecutive days OR error-rate > 1% for 48 hours, Redwood may pause the pilot and revert to standard SLOs.
5) Legal and Deal Desk: Marissa — please prepare the contract amendment language and route the revised SOW (Orbital_SOW_v3.pdf) through DocuSign. Include the Deal ID ORB-2027-019 on the amendment. Finance will record the 12% credit against the first invoice; accounting to confirm the journal entry.

This exception is authorized because Orbital is a strategic account in the US commercial pipeline; we should closely monitor telemetry and have a weekly check-in during the pilot.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
